subject: Re: Performance SLO + Concurrency / rate limit follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>, Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLO / concurrency

Hi Tom / Sandra — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) SLO targets you shared
- P95 end-to-end latency for streaming chat-style responses: < 200ms (target)
- Sustained throughput goal: ~1,500 requests/min during business hours with short spikes up to 2,500 requests/min
- Concurrency: typical steady-state concurrent requests ~400, peak concurrency ~1,200 (bursts up to ~1,500)

2) Streaming and connection behavior
- You will stream partial tokens to users and open long-lived connections from your frontends to our API (keep-alive).
- Connection pooling note: your backend uses ~200 outbound HTTP/2 connections per region; you asked about limits per connection and max concurrent request windows.

3) Redwood rate limits / quota options discussed
- Hosted default rate limits (for context): per-tenant per-region concurrent request soft limit ~200, burstable via reserved capacity (Dedicated) or quota raise.
- For your target concurrency we recommend Dedicated capacity with negotiated concurrency quotas and fallback model variants for graceful degradation.

4) Next steps / asks
- I attached a short proposal with a few capacity sizing options (see attachment). Please confirm which plan looks closest to your procurement expectations.
- Tom: can you confirm average request size (# tokens) and whether you use function calls (yes/no) for the majority of calls?
- Sandra: can you share any SLOs we should mirror in our SLA draft (availability / latency)?
- Internal: I'll loop ops to provide a formal concurrency quota proposal and a pilot timeline.

Attachments: 20270905-acme-concurrency-proposal.xlsx (size/price scenarios)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a detailed mutual action plan by EOD Friday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLO / concurrency

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Average request size is ~350 tokens in and ~150 tokens out (we stream partial tokens for UI responsiveness).
- We do use function calls for ~20% of requests (mainly for retrieval + actions).
- Our frontends maintain roughly 200 HTTP/2 connections per region as noted; each connection supports multiplexing but we do see hotspots during marketing campaigns.

On concurrency: the 1,200 peak concurrency number is accurate for peak traffic; steady-state is closer to 350-450. If we need to throttle, we'd prefer token-level shedding rather than hard connection drops.

Can you confirm whether Redwood's hosted soft limit of ~200 concurrent requests per tenant would apply per-region? We want to avoid cross-region routing surprises.

Also please send the pilot MOP (what success looks like, test plan) and an updated pricing estimate.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of AI Platform — ACME Inc.
Tom.Reynolds@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLO / concurrency (internal)

Laura / Aditya — forwarding Tom's reply. Key asks: confirm per-region concurrency behavior, pilot MOP, and updated price for a Dedicated pool sized for 1,500 req/min steady and 2,500 spike; must support peak concurrency 1,200 with streaming. 

Proposed quick plan: 
- Option A (Pilot Dedicated): reserve a small Dedicated pool (1-2 nodes depending on model) with a negotiated concurrency quota of 1,500 concurrent requests (soft limit) and emergency burst to 2,000 for 48h once during test window.
- Option B (Hosted + Quota Raise): keep ACME on Hosted but raise per-tenant concurrency quota to 1,200 per region + configure smart routing and prefix caching to reduce real concurrency. This is cheaper but has slightly higher risk for tail latency under bursts.

Engineering notes I need from you: realistic token-based concurrency-to-GPU mapping for the models we proposed (mix of 7B quantized and 16B fp16). Also confirm whether connection pooling (200 connections/region) should be handled as parallel request capacity or if we should recommend fronting via an internal aggregator.

I'll draft a one-page MOP and pricing options — can one of you take ownership of the engineering numbers by EOD tomorrow?

-Marissa
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Performance SLO / concurrency

Thanks — that sounds reasonable. We'd like to proceed with Option A (Pilot Dedicated) provided the pilot MOP includes: 

- Clear success criteria (p95 latency < 200ms, error rate < 0.2%, streaming token latency < 20ms)
- A capacity plan that supports sustained 1,500 req/min and peak concurrency 1,500 for 2 hours during our load test
- A rollback/fallback plan to a smaller model or reduced concurrency if tail latency degrades
- An initial 30-day pilot contract and an estimated monthly cost for the Dedicated pool and negotiated concurrency quota

Please send DocuSign for the pilot contract and the mutual action plan so I can get procurement moving. Also thanks for including SOC2 evidence in the drive link.

Tom
